constraints.statement: Two guardrails forbid implementation code in specs (sdd-spec.md:17) and tasks (sdd-task.md:14); change #1 cannot land without rewording them.
The premise is already accepted by the pipeline: sdd-task.md:111 says the implementing agent (Sonnet/Haiku) WILL hallucinate without explicit code anchors — the gap is mechanism, not diagnosis.

Code already appears unevenly in specs (0–384 fenced lines) and barely in tasks (1 line in the newest); the change must make explained code a structured, required deliverable rather than merely permitting it.
The Codex seat's model cannot be set from a Claude Code agent's frontmatter; it must be passed on the codex CLI (-m / -c) at invocation time.
codex-cli 0.153.4 supports stdin prompts, -m, -c model_reasoning_effort, --output-schema and -o, so the brief can be piped and the answer captured as validated JSON.
artifacts/ is gitignored; Codex design-research output must be persisted under sdd/state/<FEAT-ID>/ to be auditable from the spec and visible to worktrees.

/sdd-spec is executed unattended by sdd-planner inside the dev-loop, so the Codex phase must be optional and non-blocking (absent binary, timeout, invalid model → record 'no external design research' and continue).
Every sdd-* command has a byte-near twin in .agent/workflows/ (and agents in _subagent_data/ with a parity test); edits must be mirrored.
sdd-worker reads the whole task file and implements 'EXACTLY as specified', so richer task content is consumed with zero changes to the worker.

'Accepted' is a defined state on brainstorms and proposals; the brief to Codex is the accepted exploration doc (Problem Statement, Constraints, Recommended Option, Code Context) — never Claude's spec draft.
The requested Codex model `gpt-5.6-luna` is accepted by codex-cli 0.153.4 (probe exit 0); it becomes the verified default of SDD_DESIGN_RESEARCH_MODEL.

whats_new: A 'Collaborative Design Research' phase in /sdd-spec (new §3b, between the §2c carry-forward summary and §4 codebase research): build a neutral brief from the accepted brainstorm/proposal, run codex in the background with an explicit thinking model, parse a schema-validated JSON list of suggestions, triage each CONFIRM/REJECT/ESCALATE, fold CONFIRMed ideas into §2/§3/§7, and record the triage table in the spec.

Two new templates: sdd/templates/design_research.prompt.md (the neutral brief + question) and sdd/templates/design_research.schema.json (suggestions: id, title, rationale, affected_paths, risk, kind ∈ {architecture, api, testing, risk, alternative}).

A new spec section '§9 Design Research Cross-Check' (triage table + pointer to the raw Codex transcript under sdd/state/<FEAT-ID>/design_research/), mirroring the code-reviewer's 'Adversarial Cross-Check' report block.

A 'Reference Implementation' block per module in spec §3 (signature-level skeleton + docstrings + a short 'why' paragraph per block) and a 'Reference Implementation (starting point)' section in every task file (executor-ready skeleton, per-block explanation, explicit 'fill in' list, verified-at anchors).

A 'Explain-for-executor' writing rule in /sdd-spec and /sdd-task: every non-trivial design decision the spec makes is restated as an imperative instruction plus the reason, so a non-thinking executor does not have to infer intent.

patterns_to_follow.pattern: Neutral brief: artifact + requirements + question; withhold the primary's reasoning and draft.
Advisory triage CONFIRM / REJECT / ESCALATE with a per-finding reason table; never silently concede or drop.
Verify every path/symbol the external model cites before adopting it; unverifiable ⇒ not a finding.
Structured output via --output-schema + -o, read-only sandbox, explicit -m and -c model_reasoning_effort=high (do not rely on operator config).
Persist research state under sdd/state/<FEAT-ID>/ and commit it with the document (as /sdd-proposal does).
Every code reference carries a 'verified: path:line' anchor (Codebase Contract quality bar).

integration_risks.risk: Spec/task bloat and code drift: reference skeletons can go stale between spec and implementation.
integration_risks.mitigation: Skeleton-level only (signatures/docstrings/explained blocks), verified-at anchors, and sdd-worker's existing contract re-verification step (F013).

integration_risks.risk: Unattended planner blocks on Codex (absent binary, auth, timeout, bad model name).
integration_risks.mitigation: Phase is optional: detect `command -v codex`, 10-minute cap, on any failure write a 'no external design research' note into §9 and continue (same fallback as the review policy).

integration_risks.risk: Codex suggestions hallucinate paths/symbols and get copied into the Codebase Contract.
integration_risks.mitigation: Every CONFIRMed suggestion must be re-verified by read/grep before it enters §2/§6; REJECT with reason otherwise.

integration_risks.risk: Requested model 'gpt 5.6-luna' may not exist for codex-cli 0.153.4.
integration_risks.mitigation: Make the model a config value with a verified default; validate with a one-shot `codex exec -m <model> 'ping'` at spec time and fall back to the operator's config model.
Edit both in the same task; consider a parity check like test_subagent_parity.py for commands.

integration_risks.risk: Ratification instead of research: if the brief carries Claude's own design, Codex just agrees.
integration_risks.mitigation: Brief is built from the accepted exploration doc only; the Codex pass runs BEFORE §4/§5 drafting.

unknowns.question: Which Codex model and reasoning setting should the design-research seat use, and where is it configured?
plausible_answers: a) new env/config key SDD_DESIGN_RESEARCH_MODEL with a verified default and -c model_reasoning_effort=high (recommended)
c) no -m flag: inherit the operator's ~/.codex/config.toml (gpt-6-astra/high today)
unknowns.user_answer: gpt-5.6-luna, confirmed against the installed CLI (F017); config key SDD_DESIGN_RESEARCH_MODEL, invoked with -m and -c model_reasoning_effort=high.

unknowns.question: How should Codex's suggestions enter the spec — via an explicit CONFIRM/REJECT/ESCALATE table (§9) with CONFIRMed items folded into §2/§3/§7, or merged silently into the design?
plausible_answers: a) explicit §9 triage table + fold CONFIRMed items in place, raw transcript under sdd/state/<FEAT-ID>/design_research/ (recommended — mirrors code review)
b) silent merge, transcript only in state
c) append Codex output verbatim as an appendix, no triage
unknowns.user_answer: As recommended: explicit CONFIRM/REJECT/ESCALATE table in spec §9; CONFIRMed items folded into §2/§3/§7; transcript under sdd/state/<FEAT-ID>/design_research/.

unknowns.question: How much code is 'usable code + explanations'? Skeletons with signatures/docstrings/explained blocks, or near-complete implementations the executor mostly pastes?
plausible_answers: a) skeleton-level per module/task: signatures, docstrings, explained blocks, TODO fill-in list, verified-at anchors (recommended)
b) near-complete reference implementation per task; executor adapts and tests
c) skeletons in spec, near-complete code only in task files
unknowns.user_answer: Not the full implementation. Centre of gravity is /sdd-task: each TASK file gets an Implementation Blueprint (per-file code blocks Haiku can write to disk nearly verbatim + explanation + FILL IN list); spec keeps interface-level skeletons.

unknowns.question: Is the Codex design-research pass mandatory (fail /sdd-spec when codex is unavailable) or optional with an explicit 'no external design research' note?
plausible_answers: a) optional, non-blocking, note recorded in §9 (recommended — required for the unattended planner)
b) mandatory in interactive runs, optional under sdd-planner
unknowns.user_answer: Optional pass: skip with a recorded note when codex is absent/fails/times out.
